Henryk Sienkiewicz, Quo Vadis, translated by Jeremiah Curtin.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/henryk-sienkiewicz/quo-vadis/jeremiah-curtin

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Henryk Sienkiewicz, the author and the writer of the introduction, died 1916 (Wikidata Q41502, date of death 1916-11-15).
- Jeremiah Curtin, the annotator and the translator, died 1906 (Wikidata Q6180799, date of death 1906-12-14).

First publication of the text used: 1896 (SE colophon: 'Quo Vadis was published in 1895 by Henryk Sienkiewicz. It was translated from Polish in 1896 by Jeremiah Curtin.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1896, before 1931. The edition's own statement of rights, quoted below, says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (the country of first publication of the text, which the facts do not name): the last person to die among those named above died in 1916. So the work is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, and the country does not matter.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: first publication 1896 (quoted above).
- Wikidata Q41502 (Henryk Sienkiewicz), P570 = 1916-11-15.
- Wikidata Q6180799 (Jeremiah Curtin), P570 = 1906-12-14.
